name: minimal
description: Minimal API style rules based on common REST best practices. A lightweight profile for basic API hygiene.

categories.title: URI Design
categories.description: Rules for URL structure and naming

categories.title: HTTP Methods
categories.description: Rules for proper HTTP method usage

categories.title: Naming Conventions
categories.description: Rules for property and parameter naming

rules.title: Use plural resource names
rules.rationale: Plural resource names provide consistency and clearly indicate collections. Use /users instead of /user.

judge.prompt: Check if all top-level resource names in paths use plural form (e.g., /users not /user).

rules.title: Use kebab-case for path segments
rules.rationale: Kebab-case (lowercase with hyphens) is the standard for URLs. Avoid camelCase or snake_case in paths.

rules.title: Avoid verbs in paths
rules.rationale: REST uses HTTP methods to indicate actions. Avoid verbs like /getUsers or /createOrder in paths.

rules.title: Use path parameters for resource identifiers
rules.rationale: Resource identifiers should be path parameters, not query parameters. Use /users/{id} not /users?id=123.

judge.prompt: Check if resource identifiers are properly placed in path parameters rather than query parameters.

rules.title: Limit path nesting depth
rules.rationale: Deeply nested paths are hard to read and maintain. Limit nesting to 3 levels (e.g., /a/{id}/b/{id}/c).

rules.title: GET requests must not have request body
rules.rationale: GET requests should be safe and idempotent. Request bodies are not semantically defined for GET.

rules.title: DELETE requests should not have request body
rules.rationale: DELETE requests typically don't need a body. The resource to delete is identified by the URL.

rules.title: POST should return 201 for resource creation
rules.rationale: When POST creates a new resource, return 201 Created with a Location header, not 200 OK.

rules.title: Use PATCH for partial updates
rules.rationale: PATCH is for partial updates, PUT is for full replacement. Use PATCH when updating specific fields.

judge.prompt: Check if the API properly distinguishes between PATCH (partial update) and PUT (full replacement).

rules.title: Operations must have unique operationId
rules.rationale: Each operation needs a unique operationId for code generation and documentation.

rules.title: Use camelCase for JSON properties
rules.rationale: camelCase is the JavaScript/JSON convention. Use firstName, not first_name or FirstName.

rules.title: Use camelCase for query parameters
rules.rationale: Query parameters should follow the same camelCase convention as JSON properties.

rules.title: Boolean properties should use is/has/can prefix
rules.rationale: Boolean properties are clearer with prefixes like isActive, hasPermission, canEdit.

judge.prompt: Check if boolean schema properties use appropriate prefixes (is, has, can, should, will).

rules.title: Use consistent date/time property naming
rules.rationale: Use consistent suffixes for timestamps: createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt, expiresAt.

judge.prompt: Check if date/time properties use consistent naming like createdAt, updatedAt with At suffix.

rules.title: Define error responses for operations
rules.rationale: Operations should define expected error responses (4xx, 5xx) for proper client handling.

judge.prompt: Check if operations define appropriate error responses (400, 401, 403, 404, 500).

rules.title: Use consistent error response schema
rules.rationale: Error responses should follow a consistent format, preferably RFC 7807 Problem Details.

judge.prompt: Check if error responses follow RFC 7807 Problem Details format with type, title, status, detail fields.

rules.title: Include 401 response for authenticated endpoints
rules.rationale: Endpoints requiring authentication should document the 401 Unauthorized response.

judge.prompt: Check if endpoints with security requirements define a 401 response.

rules.title: Responses must have descriptions
rules.rationale: Each response should have a description explaining what it represents.

rules.title: Success responses should define content schema
rules.rationale: Success responses (2xx) should define the response body schema for code generation.

rules.title: Use consistent pagination format
rules.rationale: List endpoints should use consistent pagination with standard fields like items, totalCount, nextCursor.

judge.prompt: Check if list/collection responses use consistent pagination format across the API.

rules.title: API must have info description
rules.rationale: The info section should have a description explaining the API's purpose.

rules.title: Operations must have summary or description
rules.rationale: Each operation should have a summary or description explaining what it does.

rules.title: Parameters must have descriptions
rules.rationale: Parameters should have descriptions explaining their purpose and valid values.

rules.title: Schema properties should have descriptions
rules.rationale: Schema properties benefit from descriptions, especially for complex or non-obvious fields.

judge.prompt: Check if schema properties have descriptions, especially for non-obvious fields.

rules.title: Provide examples for schemas
rules.rationale: Examples help consumers understand expected data formats and valid values.

judge.prompt: Check if schemas provide examples for key types and properties.

rules.title: Define security schemes
rules.rationale: APIs should define security schemes in components.securitySchemes.

rules.title: Apply security to operations
rules.rationale: Operations should specify security requirements either globally or per-operation.

judge.prompt: Check if operations have security requirements defined globally or per-operation.

rules.title: Avoid API keys in URL
rules.rationale: API keys in URLs are logged and cached. Use headers instead.

rules.title: Use HTTPS for server URLs
rules.rationale: All API server URLs should use HTTPS for secure communication.

bronze.description: Minimum viable API - basic structure and methods

silver.description: Production-ready API - proper naming and error handling

gold.description: Exemplary API - complete documentation and security
